_meta.description: Publication-ready benchmark naming map for TCTL tableau solver evaluation

A1_untimed.phenomenon: Alternating AG/EF nesting without clocks, isolating structural depth cost from timed operations
A1_untimed.rationale: This benchmark provides an untimed control by alternating AG and EF operators around a single atom, measuring pure structural depth overhead without any zone operations.

A2_overlap_sat.phenomenon: Conjunction of bounded EF obligations with overlapping timing windows and fresh atoms per conjunct
A2_overlap_sat.rationale: Each conjunct introduces a clock with an overlapping window, forcing zone interaction; fresh atoms prevent trivial zone collapse. The satisfiable verdict confirms a witness exists.

A3_nested_eu.phenomenon: Deeply nested timed EU operators with fresh atoms per layer, forcing simultaneous clock tracking and eventuality checking
A3_nested_eu.rationale: Each nesting level allocates a fresh clock and requires eventuality fulfilment, preventing early closure and exercising the tableau's zone-eventuality interaction.

A4_killed_unsat.phenomenon: Overlapping EF obligations rendered unsatisfiable by a universally quantified AG negation of all target atoms
A4_killed_unsat.rationale: Layering a timed AG constraint that negates every obligation atom forces the solver to individually refute each EF, exercising exhaustive search and zone-contradiction detection.

B1_EU_delay.phenomenon: Single bounded EU requiring symbolic time progression before satisfaction
B1_EU_delay.rationale: The formula E(¬p₀ U[0,M] p₀) forces a non-trivial time advance before the target holds, measuring how growing M affects zone operations.

B2_deadline_unsat.phenomenon: Contradictory timing constraints: a global prohibition AG[0,M] ¬p₀ versus a bounded reachability EF[1,M] p₀
B2_deadline_unsat.rationale: The safety constraint globally forbids p₀ within the same window where an eventuality demands it, creating a structural contradiction the solver must detect across all zones.

B3_negated_window.phenomenon: Self-contradictory conjunction of a timed modality and its own negation, stressing normalization of negated bounded operators
B3_negated_window.rationale: EF[0,M] p₀ ∧ ¬EF[0,M] p₀ is immediately contradictory; this tests the solver's ability to detect propositional-level timed contradictions efficiently.

B4_chain_windows.phenomenon: Fixed-structure chain of consecutive EF windows whose endpoints scale with M, isolating the effect of growing interval constants
B4_chain_windows.rationale: With fixed k=5 conjuncts and windows partitioning [0,M], only the numeric constants grow, tightening M-abstraction and forcing finer zone distinctions as M increases.

B5_nested_chain.phenomenon: Fixed-depth nested EU chain where only the interval bound M varies, isolating max-constant impact on zone complexity
B5_nested_chain.rationale: Six nested EU operators with interval [0,M] keep the structural depth constant while raising max_constants_ per clock, stressing the extrapolation mechanism.

B6_forced_delay.phenomenon: Tight interval EF[M−1,M] p₀ requiring symbolic time advance to at least M−1, with zone extrapolation enabled
B6_forced_delay.rationale: The narrow window forces time to reach M−1 before p₀ can hold; with extrapolation ON, M-abstraction keeps zone count bounded regardless of M's growth.

B6_forced_delay_noextr.phenomenon: Same formula as B6 but with zone extrapolation disabled, measuring the ablation impact of M-abstraction
B6_forced_delay_noextr.rationale: Disabling extrapolation removes the finiteness guarantee on zones, causing the zone count to grow with M and demonstrating the necessity of M-abstraction for termination.

C1_staggered.phenomenon: k conjunctive EF obligations with staggered (non-overlapping) timing windows and fresh atoms
C1_staggered.rationale: Each obligation's window EF[i, i+2] uses a distinct interval, forcing the solver to track k independent clocks with non-overlapping timing constraints.

C2_overlapping.phenomenon: k conjunctive EF obligations sharing the same timing window [1,3] but with distinct target atoms
C2_overlapping.rationale: Sharing the identical interval maximises zone overlap potential, testing whether the solver's zone operations can exploit structural redundancy when windows coincide.

until_nested.phenomenon: Progressive nesting of existential bounded-until operators with a fixed interval
until_nested.rationale: Each additional nesting level allocates a clock and an eventuality obligation, measuring the cost of increasing until-depth while max-constant remains fixed.

until_conjunctive.phenomenon: Conjunction of independent bounded-EU obligations, widening the formula rather than deepening it
until_conjunctive.source_location: benchmark.cpp:1048–1054 (inline generator in Family D loop); curves_until_release_mixed.csv; plot2_depth_complexity
until_conjunctive.rationale: This variant grows formula width (distinct EU conjuncts) rather than depth, isolating the cost of concurrent eventuality tracking versus nested operator expansion.

release_nested.phenomenon: Progressive nesting of existential bounded-release operators, testing greatest-fixpoint handling at increasing depth
release_nested.rationale: Release (greatest fixpoint) requires continuous preservation rather than eventuality fulfilment, creating a dual stress pattern to nested-until for the tableau's fixpoint handling.

mixed.phenomenon: Conjunction of nested-until and nested-release subformulas, forcing simultaneous least- and greatest-fixpoint resolution
mixed.rationale: Combining both fixpoint types in a single formula creates the worst-case for the tableau, which must simultaneously satisfy eventuality obligations (until) and preservation requirements (release).

F1_ag_false.phenomenon: AG[1,M] false: vacuously satisfiable under Zeno semantics but correctly unsatisfiable under time-divergent acceptance
F1_ag_false.rationale: Under Zeno semantics, time never reaches [1,M], making the AG vacuously true; the solver must detect that all non-Zeno runs falsify AG, correctly reporting UNSAT.

F2_eg_conflict.phenomenon: EG p₀ ∧ AG[1,M] ¬p₀: the infinite EG path with p₀ conflicts with the timed AG prohibiting p₀ in [1,M], detectable only under non-Zeno acceptance
F2_eg_conflict.rationale: A Zeno loop keeps time below 1, avoiding the AG window; the solver must reject this loop and verify that all time-divergent paths lead to a contradiction between p₀ and ¬p₀.

F3_stacked_zeno.phenomenon: k simultaneous AG/EG contradictions creating a multi-clock Zeno trap whose complexity grows with M
F3_stacked_zeno.rationale: As M increases, k=M−1 obligations each allocate a clock, scaling both the zone dimension and the number of contradictions the anti-Zeno check must verify simultaneously.

G1_conjunctive.phenomenon: k staggered EF obligations with fresh atoms, forcing k concurrent clocks and O(k²) zone operations per step
G1_conjunctive.rationale: Staggered intervals prevent zone collapse and force the DBM dimension to k+1, measuring the quadratic cost of zone operations as clock count grows.

G2_nested.phenomenon: k-deep nested EU chain keeping all outer clocks active, preventing early clock deallocation
G2_nested.rationale: Nesting prevents any clock from being freed until the innermost eventuality is resolved, maximising simultaneous active-clock count and stressing the zone engine.

G3_killed.phenomenon: Same k-clock structure as G1 but with a universal AG killer rendering all obligations unsatisfiable
G3_killed.rationale: Adding AG[0, M+k](¬p₁ ∧ … ∧ ¬pₖ) forces full search-space exploration at each clock dimension, measuring UNSAT cost as k grows.

H1_chain_eu.phenomenon: n-deep chain of existential bounded-until operators with fixed small M, isolating formula length from max-constant effects
H1_chain_eu.rationale: Holding M=2 fixed, all growth comes from the chain length n; each level adds a fresh clock and atom, measuring how the number of simultaneous eventualities affects solver cost.

H2_chain_killed.phenomenon: Same EU chain as H1 but conjoined with AG ¬q, forcing exhaustive search since the terminal eventuality can never be fulfilled
H2_chain_killed.rationale: The global AG ¬q prevents any EU chain from terminating successfully, forcing the solver to exhaust all branches and measuring worst-case search cost per chain length.

I1_pure_safety.phenomenon: n nested universal timed release operators, testing greatest-fixpoint-only cost without eventuality overhead
I1_pure_safety.rationale: Using only AR (release/safety), no pending eventualities accumulate; this provides a baseline showing the cost of pure greatest-fixpoint nesting at depth n.

I2_pure_liveness.phenomenon: n nested universal timed until operators, requiring n simultaneous eventuality fulfilments
I2_pure_liveness.rationale: Using only AU (until/liveness), every nesting level creates an eventuality obligation the tableau must discharge, measuring the cost of accumulating least-fixpoint obligations.

I3_alternating.phenomenon: Interleaved universal until and release operators, creating a worst-case alternation between least- and greatest-fixpoint obligations
I3_alternating.rationale: Alternating U/R forces the loop-acceptance check to handle competing eventualities and safety constraints simultaneously, representing the hardest case for fixpoint reasoning.
